statement: Let $f(x)=x^{3}-3x$. Find the coordinates of its turning points. The restriction of $f$ to $x\\ge1$ is one-to-one; let $g$ be its inverse. Find $g'(2)$.
solution: $f'(x)=3x^{2}-3=3(x^{2}-1)$, zero at $x=\\pm1$. Since $f''(x)=6x$, $x=1$ gives a minimum with $f(1)=-2$ and $x=-1$ gives a maximum with $f(-1)=2$; turning points $(1,-2)$ and $(-1,2)$. For the inverse on $x\\ge1$: $g(2)$ satisfies $f(g(2))=2$, i.e. $x^{3}-3x-2=0$, which factors as $(x-2)(x+1)^{2}=0$, so $g(2)=2$. By the inverse-function rule, $g'(2)=1/f'(g(2))=1/f'(2)=1/(3\\cdot4-3)=1/9$.
hints: Use f'' to classify each turning point.
Solve f(x)=2 to get g(2), then use g'(y)=1/f'(g(y)).
